requirements_summary: Enterprise trading platform; latency first. Primary workload: conversational trading assistant + inline reranking for signals. Require Dedicated GPUs in VPC; require clear p50/p95/p99 definitions across streaming and non-streaming paths. Need server-side breakdown for ops and client-side E2E SLO for legal/ops. Throughput guarantee for market hours (10:00-18:00 EST) with burst capacity in first 30 minutes of open. Must support SSO and strict retention and residency controls.
notes:
SLO alignment / measurement discussion (notes + shorthand):
- Customer emphasis: 'latency is the product' — will baseline UX to p95.
- Definitions: p50/p95/p99 to be computed on end-to-end client observed request-to-last-byte (primary SLA metric). Server-side percentiles used for troubleshooting only.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: agreed split:
  * Non-streaming (single response): measure total server decode completed -> client received last byte. For SLA, use client-side end-to-end elapsed.
  * Streaming (token-by-token): SLA for first-byte latency (time to first partial token) + tail for stream stability (p95 of time-to-first-byte and p99 of inter-token gap). Also include 'session-keepalive' metric to capture mid-stream stalls.
- Client vs server timing: quantica insists on E2E for contracts. We propose dual reporting: E2E (client header) + annotated server breakdown (x-queue-ms, x-infer-ms, x-decode-ms, x-net-egress-ms). Instrumentation will add these headers to responses for each request to allow reconciliation.
- Percentile windows & SLA cadence: rolling 7-day window for operational alerts, 30-day window for SLA compliance calculation. Monthly crediting for missed SLA with agreed exclusions (scheduled maintenance, customer traffic surges above defined peak).
- Measurement caveats: clock skew, CDN/proxy buffering, and client-side network variance. Plan: require sync time source on client test agents and collect both client and server timestamps. Provide reconciler script.
- Streaming considerations: recommend WebSocket or TLS chunked + heartbeat to reduce proxy buffering. Test matrix to include client variants (web, mobile, internal API).
- Reserved GPU planning heuristics discussed:
  * Base throughput assumptions (example numbers for scoping): A100-80GB ~ 120k tokens/sec for generation at batch=32 / mix of prompt lengths. T4-class ~ 12-20k tokens/sec.
  * Sizing formula (agreed): GPUs_needed = ceil((peak_RPS * avg_tokens_per_request) / tokens_per_gpu_per_sec * safety_factor). Safety_factor default 1.4 for production.
  * Concurrency and batch sizing: recommend conservative batch target to keep tail down; cap batching window at 20ms for low-latency workloads.
  * KV cache recommendations for chat: pin sessions to GPU pool when possible to reduce prompt growth and decoding time.
- Throughput guarantees: Quantica wants 95% of market-hours requests served without queuing beyond 10ms. We proposed two-tier capacity: reserved baseline (covering 90% load) + burst pool (pay-per-use) for spikes.
- SLA negotiation points: credits for p95 and p99 breaches, scheduled maintenance windows, definitions for force majeure and traffic shaping. Customer requested allowance for model upgrades (they want advance notice + can opt in/out to variants).
- Test plan / acceptance criteria:
  1) Run three 2-hour synthetic runs matching customer traffic patterns (session lengths, inter-arrival) from their VPC egress.
  2) Validate E2E p50/p95/p99 targets under stable and spike scenarios.
  3) Confirm streaming first-byte and sustained stream stability metrics.
  4) Run model rollback & fallback to smaller quantized variant; measure failover latency.
- Operational tooling: enable per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, trace links for slow requests. Add automatic alerting for queue growth (percent queued / second).
- Risks called out: enterprise peak degeneracy during open can cause high tail if batching backpressure not applied. Need feature gating on adaptive batching.
- Pricing sensitivity: they asked for a blended committed spend (reserved GPUs + lower per-token for hosted fallback).
